# Stargate

Williams' 1981 arcade game: the same pictures, colors, sounds, motion and rules, checked
against the arcade, frame by frame, as MAME emulates it.

The shape to notice:

- **The game is a dataset with its own rules.** `Game` (game.declare) holds what is on and
  above the planet as records, and the rules they share. Each kind of thing has a part of
  the game of its own, in its own file, saying what it does on its turn and what becomes
  of it when hit: men.declare, landers.declare, firebombers.declare, dynamos.declare. The
  ship, its buttons and its laser are ship.declare; the director that stages a wave is
  director.declare; the planet's ground, stars and scanner are scenery.declare; the pages
  shown between games are pages.declare, drawn by page-views.declare.
- **Things act in turns.** Each turn does a little and then waits some passes; what it does
  next is its step, and each step is a method of its kind's rules, so a lander's life
  reads as cruise, seek, flee, drawIn, hunt (rules.declare, landers.declare).
- **The arcade's own timing is kept apart.** How its processor fits the game's work into
  each frame, and the leftovers in its memory that a few rules read, are clock.declare and
  memory.declare. None of it is a rule of the game, but without it the game would not be the arcade's.
- **The screen follows the data.** Each part of the screen is a view class
  (screen.declare, panel.declare) drawn from the records; nothing in the views changes
  anything. The arcade's monitor redraws each half of the playfield while its beam is in the
  other, so the top is a frame older than the bottom. `Monitor` (screen.declare) can draw it
  that way, as the frame-by-frame comparison with MAME needs; in play the whole playfield is
  drawn from the world as each frame ends.
- **Places are pixels**, kept to the fractions of a pixel the arcade moves things by: across
  a planet 2,048 pixels round, and down the screen (game.declare says more).

Keys: Q up, A down, ' thrust, Return fire, Z reverse, Space hyperspace, / smart bomb,
; inviso. Return or Space starts a game; Escape pauses.

*This program is new code, written in Declare. It recreates the behavior of Stargate, Williams
Electronics' 1981 arcade game, whose original program was written in Motorola 6809 assembly
language, and reproduces its look and sound as closely as it can, frame by frame. Stargate, its
name, artwork, sounds and visual design belong to Williams Electronics, Inc. or its successors;
they are used here only to illustrate and test the Declare language, and no claim is made to
them. The MIT license of this repository covers this code, not the original game's name,
artwork or sounds. If you hold rights in this material and object to its being posted here,
please open an issue on this repository on GitHub, or message me there, and I will remove it.*

script {
    // the host's clock, in milliseconds, for measuring how long the rules take
    function wallClock(): number { return performance.now() }
    }

include [ "game.declare", "screen.declare", "panel.declare", "page-views.declare", "../touch-pad.declare" ]

defaultFlags [ render = canvas, accessibility = false ]

App [ appName = "Stargate", fill = black,

    shapes: DataSource [ url = "art/shapes.json", auto = true ],
    pictures: Image [ visible = false, source = "art/pictures.png" ],   // every picture, one under another
    ready: boolean = { app.shapes.loaded && app.pictures.loaded && app.game.scenery.ground.loaded },     // all the art is in
    letters: Letters [ ],

    game: Game [
        shapes = { app.shapes.value ?? {} }     // the pictures' sizes and outlines, once loaded
        ] { {
        "seen": { "scroll": 0, "lastScroll": 0, "shipShown": false, "shipGlows": false, "wiped": true, "groundShown": false,
            "groundAt": 0, "colors": [], "rings": [0, 0, 0], "shotLook": 1 },
        "ship": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "speed": 0, "climb": 0, "facing": 1, "turnTo": 1,
            "px": 0, "py": 0, "nextPy": 0, "flame": [], "planetX": 0 },
        "near": [],
        "far": [],
        "men": [],
        "shots": [],
        "turns": [],
        "appears": [],
        "bursts": [],
        "trails": [],
        "stars": [],
        "rocks": [],
        "scan": { "blips": [], "ground": -1, "shipPx": 0, "shipPy": 0 },
        "shards": [],
        "lost": []
        } },

    speaker: Speaker [ board = { app.game.board }, quiet = { app.paused } ],

    monitor: Monitor [ game = { app.game } ],

    // the arcade's controls, on the keyboard or the touch screen

    controls() -> Controls {
        const down = (key: string, button: string) => (Keys.isDown(key) && key != app.heldBack) || app.pad.isDown(button)
        return { up: down("KeyQ", "up"), down: down("KeyA", "down"), thrust: down("Quote", "thrust"), reverse: down("KeyZ", "reverse"),
            fire: down("Enter", "fire"), smartBomb: down("Slash", "smartBomb"), hyperspace: down("Space", "hyperspace"),
            inviso: down("Semicolon", "inviso") }
        },

    // Return or Space starts a game when none is being played. Escape pauses a game, and any
    // key goes on with it. A key that starts or resumes does only that: its own part in the
    // game waits until it is let go and pressed again.

    paused: boolean = false,
    heldBack: string = "",
    keys: Keys [
        onKeyDown(e: KeyEvent) {
            app.restCursor()
            if (e.repeat || e.meta || e.ctrl || e.alt) return
            if (app.paused && !app.game.gameOver) { app.paused = false; app.heldBack = e.code; return }
            if (e.code == "Escape" && !app.game.gameOver) { app.paused = true; return }
            if ((e.code == "Enter" || e.code == "Space") && app.game.gameOver) { app.heldBack = e.code; app.game.start() }
            if (e.code == "F2") app.timing = !app.timing
            },
        onKeyUp(e: KeyEvent) { if (e.code == app.heldBack) app.heldBack = "" }
        ],

    // In a game the cursor is hidden over the screen, and comes back when the game ends, when
    // it is paused, or when the mouse moves more than 10 pixels. A key hides it again.

    cursor = { !app.game.gameOver && !app.paused && !app.mouseMoved ? "none" : "" },
    mouseMoved: boolean = false,
    restX: number = 0,                  // where the pointer was at the last key
    restY: number = 0,
    restCursor() { mouseMoved = false; restX = pointerX; restY = pointerY },
    trackChanges = ["pointerX", "pointerY"],
    onChange(e: ChangeEvent) {
        if (Math.abs(pointerX - restX) > 10 || Math.abs(pointerY - restY) > 10) mouseMoved = true
        },

    // The arcade moves the game on a frame every 16.64 ms. Where a whole number of the
    // display's frames comes within 5% of that, as at 60 Hz and its multiples, the game moves
    // on every that many display frames; on any other display, time banks between display
    // frames and the game moves on every 16.64 ms of it.

    clock: Time [ tick = frame, running = { app.ready && !app.paused },
        period: number = 0.01664,
        frameTime: number = 0,          // the display's frame, averaged, in seconds
        shown: number = 0,              // display frames since the game last moved on
        banked: number = 0,
        onTick(dt: number) {
            const started = wallClock()
            for (let n = this.gameFrames(dt); n > 0; n--) app.game.step(app.controls())
            if (app.timing) app.meter.add(dt * 1000, wallClock() - started)
            },
        gameFrames(dt: number) -> number {
            if (frameTime == 0) frameTime = dt
            else if (dt < 1.5 * frameTime) frameTime = 0.95 * frameTime + 0.05 * dt
            const per = Math.max(1, Math.round(period / frameTime))
            if (Math.abs(per * frameTime - period) <= 0.05 * period) {
                shown = shown + Math.max(1, Math.round(dt / frameTime))
                const n = Math.floor(shown / per)
                shown = shown - n * per
                return n
                }
            banked = banked + dt
            const n = Math.floor(banked / period)
            banked = banked - n * period
            return n
            }
        ],

    // A whole number of display pixels to each of the arcade's, as many as fit.

    unit: number = { Math.max(1, Math.floor(Math.min(app.width / 292, app.height / 240))) },

    // The arcade's picture is 304 pixels by 256, of which its monitor shows 292 by 240, from
    // the seventh pixel across and the eighth down. It is drawn in the arcade's own pixels and
    // scaled up. Its playfield is drawn once, from the world as the frame ends — or, drawn as
    // the arcade's monitor shows it (Monitor), twice, the top half from the world as it was a
    // frame ago — and the top of the screen goes over it. Every pixel of it shows as a solid
    // block, as on the monitor.

    screen: View [ clip = true, x = center, y = center, width = 292, height = 240, scale = { app.unit }, imageSmoothing = pixelated,
        beam: number = 128,             // the row where the halves meet
        picture: View [ x = -6, y = -7, width = 304, height = 256,
            whole: Playfield [ exists = { !app.monitor.split }, datapath = { app.game.value }, explosions = { app.game } ],
            upper: View [ exists = { app.monitor.split }, clip = true, width = 100%, height = { app.screen.beam },
                Playfield [ datapath = { app.monitor.upper.value }, explosions = { app.monitor.upperBursts } ]
                ],
            lower: View [ exists = { app.monitor.split }, clip = true, width = 100%, y = { app.screen.beam }, height = { 256 - app.screen.beam },
                Playfield [ datapath = { app.game.value }, explosions = { app.monitor.lowerBursts },
                    y = { -app.screen.beam } ]
                ],
            panel: Panel [ visible = { app.game.setPieces.topShown && app.game.pages.panelShown }, score = { app.game.score },
                ships = { app.game.shipsLeft }, bombs = { app.game.smartBombs }, inviso = { app.game.invisoLeft },
                playing = { !app.game.gameOver },
                frameInk = { app.game.pages.frameColor >= 0 ? app.game.pages.frameColor : this.frameFor(app.game.director.frameWave) },
                message = { app.game.messages.strip }, messageNumber = { app.game.messages.stripNumber },
                added = { app.game.messages.stripAdded } ],

            // what is lettered across the playfield, and the men counted for a bonus under it

            banners: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, datapath = { app.lettered.value },
                Phrase [ datapath = :banners[], says = :says, number = :number, px = :px, py = :py, font = "large" ]
                ],
            bonusMen: View [ x = 112, y = 160, datapath = { app.lettered.value },
                inks: number[] = { app.game.colors },          // what the men's pictures are drawn in, as on the playfield
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 4 ],
                Sprite [ datapath = :men[], picture = "man-right-1", fill = null ]
                ],

            // the pages between games (pages.declare, page-views.declare)

            pageWords: PageWords [ visible = { app.game.pages.page != "" } ],

            // paused: the screen dimmed, and the word in the large letters, white, above the
            // middle of the playfield

            View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, fill = black, opacity = 0.6, visible = { app.paused } ],
            Lettering [ visible = { app.paused }, text = "PAUSED", font = "large", px = 132, py = 118,
                colors = { [app.game.black, app.game.white] }, ink = 1, opaque = false ]
            ]
        ],
    lettered: Dataset [ contents = { { banners: app.game.messages.banners,
        men: Array.from({ length: app.game.director.menPaid }, (unused, i) => ({ id: i })) } } ],

    // F2 shows how the browser is keeping up: the display's frames over the last second, the
    // longest of them, and the time the game's rules took in each.

    timing: boolean = false,
    meter: Node [
        frames: number[] = [],
        rules: number[] = [],
        shown: string = "",
        add(frame: number, rule: number) {
            frames = [...frames, frame]
            rules = [...rules, rule]
            if (frames.length < 60) return
            const mean = (list: number[]) => list.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / list.length
            shown = `frame ${mean(frames).toFixed(1)} ms, longest ${Math.max(...frames).toFixed(1)} ms; rules ${mean(rules).toFixed(2)} ms`
            frames = []; rules = []
            }
        ],
    readout: Text [ visible = { app.timing }, x = 8, y = 8, fontSize = 12, textColor = white, text = { app.meter.shown } ],

    // On a touch screen, the arcade's controls as its panel has them: the stick's up and down
    // and reverse under the left hand; thrust and fire under the right, with smart bomb and
    // hyperspace above them; inviso between (../touch-pad.declare). Start begins a game; over
    // the screen, it sits low on the left, off the pages' words.

    pad: TouchPad [ startShown = { app.game.gameOver }, ink = #8C8C8C, startInk = white, startOverLeft = true,
        fieldX = { app.screen.x }, fieldY = { app.screen.y },
        fieldW = { app.screen.width * app.screen.scale }, fieldH = { app.screen.height * app.screen.scale },
        buttonDown(id: string) { if (id == "start" && app.game.gameOver) app.game.start() },
        keys = { [
            { id: "up", label: "▲", side: "left", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "down", label: "▼", side: "left", col: 0, row: 1 },
            { id: "reverse", label: "REVERSE", side: "left", col: 1, row: 1 },
            { id: "inviso", label: "INVISO", side: "center", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "smartBomb", label: "SMART BOMB", side: "right", col: 0, row: 0 },
            { id: "hyperspace", label: "HYPER SPACE", side: "right", col: 1, row: 0 },
            { id: "thrust", label: "THRUST", side: "right", col: 0, row: 1 },
            { id: "fire", label: "FIRE", side: "right", col: 1, row: 1 }
            ] }
        ]
    ]
